patients.summary: Healthy IT support specialist and freelance designer who joined in 2023. A right dorsal wrist ganglion was confirmed by orthopaedics in December 2024, went away on its own, and recurred in June 2026 after his last practice visit; he chose observation.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is 25, lives in Florence, looking for a new primary care doctor. Employer plan is BCBS PPO, card info taken. Went over the membership model and the annual fee; he wants to sign on. New patient physical booked 9/12 at 8:30. Asked him to sign a release for his old primary care office so we can pull records. Consent form and intake questionnaire sent through the portal.

documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25M here to establish; previously seen at another primary care office. Works in IT support and also takes freelance graphic design work in the evenings. Feels well. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations.
PSH: none.
Meds: none, no supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: father has high blood pressure, well controlled on treatment. Mother has an underactive thyroid. No cancer in the family that he knows of, no autoimmune or rheumatologic disease.
Social: single, lives in Florence. Never smoked, no vaping. Has a drink maybe once or twice a month when out with friends. No drug use. Exercises a few times a week. Spends most of the day at a desk.
Vaccines: thinks he had a tetanus booster in his late teens or early twenties; will confirm from old records.

ROS: negative across systems on the intake form, reviewed with him.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal, TMs clear, no thyromegaly or adenopathy. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without concerning lesions. Extremities warm, full range of motion all joints, no swelling. Neuro grossly intact, gait normal. Mood and affect normal.

Assessment/plan:
1. Adult health exam, healthy 25-year-old male. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids drawn today. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, discussed and he agrees.
2. PHQ-2 is 0.
3. Immunizations: will verify the Tdap date from prior records. Flu and COVID once this season's supply is in; nurse visit in October.
4. Records release signed, request sent to prior office.
Follow up yearly, or text me with anything in between.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Zachary, everything from Tuesday came back fine. Blood counts, kidney and liver numbers and blood sugar are all normal, cholesterol is in a good range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Nothing to do. Good to meet you.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thanks for the quick turnaround!

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Eleven pages from his previous primary care office, covering 2016 through 2022. Mostly yearly physicals as a college student and young adult, all unremarkable. No chronic diagnoses, no prescriptions on file. Allergies listed as none known. Immunization record shows childhood series complete and Tdap given 06/18/2019; entered into our immunization history. No labs of note. Filed to media and routed to PCP.

PCP addendum: reviewed. Nothing to add to his problem list. Tdap current until 2029.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in after work for vaccines. No fever or illness today, no prior reactions, no allergies. Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left arm, Moderna 2023-24 COVID 0.5 mL IM right arm. VIS sheets reviewed. Sat for 15 minutes, felt fine, left ambulatory. Told him a sore arm and a tired day afterward are common.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt texted that a server migration at work moved to tomorrow morning and he can't get away. Cancelled the 9/10 physical, rebooked 9/24 at 8:00.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. Doing well. Work has been busy, a lot of screen time between the help desk and design jobs in the evening. Exercises a few times a week. No meds, NKDA. No change in family history. Never smoker, alcohol rare.

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable. Eyes, ears and throat normal. Neck supple. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Upper extremities with full strength and normal reflexes. Skin clear.

A/P:
- Health maintenance in a healthy 26-year-old. Labs from last fall were normal; no repeat needed this year.
- Desk work: talked through monitor height, a chair with lumbar support, and getting up every hour. Nothing to treat.
- PHQ-2 negative.
- Flu vaccine given today. He'll get the updated COVID shot at his pharmacy if he wants it.
See him next year.

documents.title: Bump on my wrist
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey, for the past three weeks or so there's been a small lump on the top of my right wrist, kind of squishy. Doesn't hurt at all and I didn't bang it on anything. Probably nothing but it's my mouse hand so I figured I'd ask. Can I come in sometime next week? Not urgent.

documents.title: RE: Bump on my wrist
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the heads-up. Painless and soft is reassuring. Let's take a look; the front desk will text you a time next Tuesday. If it gets red, hot or painful before then, or your fingers go numb, let me know sooner.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

orders.reason: right dorsal wrist mass, probable ganglion

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Right-handed. About 3 weeks of a soft lump on the back of the right wrist. Painless. No injury he can recall. No numbness, tingling or weakness in the hand. Doesn't limit typing or mousing. No fevers, no other joint complaints.

O: Vitals as charted. Right wrist: soft, mobile swelling on the dorsal side, not tender, no redness or warmth, skin intact. Full wrist flexion and extension. Radial pulse normal, capillary refill brisk. Sensation intact in the median, ulnar and radial distributions; grip strong. Left wrist normal.

A/P: Right dorsal wrist mass, most consistent with a ganglion. Benign appearance. He would like a hand specialist to confirm it and talk options, which is reasonable. Referral to orthopaedic surgery (hand) placed. Fine to keep working normally in the meantime; no need to try to burst it.

documents.title: Referral to Orthopaedic Surgery
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Re: Zachary Sawyer, DOB 02/26/1998

Referring this healthy 26-year-old for evaluation of a painless soft mass over the dorsal right wrist, present about 3 weeks, no trauma. Neurovascular exam normal in our office. Suspect a ganglion; he would like a specialist opinion and to hear about options. No medications. NKDA. Recent office note attached.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Orthopaedic Surgery Consultation
documents.author: orthopaedic surgery
documents.body:
Orthopaedic Surgery, Hand and Upper Extremity
Date of visit: 12/17/2024
Reason for referral: right wrist mass

Thank you for sending Mr. Sawyer, a 26-year-old right-hand-dominant man, for a swelling over the dorsum of his right wrist. He first noticed it roughly a month ago. It has never hurt and he thinks it has stayed the same size for the last couple of weeks, though it looks bigger by evening. His work in IT support and design keeps him on a keyboard and mouse much of the day. He denies any injury, weakness or numbness, and it is not getting in the way of anything he does. No fevers, weight loss or systemic illness.

Past medical history: none. Surgical history: none. Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with treated hypertension, mother with hypothyroidism; no rheumatologic disease or malignancy in the family.
Social: never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks a month.

Examination: Right wrist without tenderness. Active and passive motion are full. Over the dorsal wrist there is a 2 cm soft swelling with smooth, distinct borders. It moves freely beneath the skin and palpation causes no discomfort. Skin over it is normal in color and temperature, and it is not fluctuant. Neurologic exam of both upper limbs is normal.

Impression: Dorsal ganglion cyst, right wrist.

Plan: We reviewed that this is a benign, fluid-filled cyst arising from the joint or tendon sheath, common in his age group, and that many shrink or disappear without treatment. No imaging is needed. Given that it is painless and not limiting, we agreed on observation. He may return if it enlarges, becomes painful, or bothers him enough to consider aspiration or removal.

Sincerely,
Orthopaedic Surgery, Hand Service

documents.title: Hand surgery letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Zachary, I got the letter from the hand surgeon. Same read as ours: a ganglion cyst, nothing dangerous. Watching it is a perfectly good plan, and plenty of these go away on their own. Reach out if it starts to hurt or grows.

documents.title: RE: Hand surgery letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Yep, that's what they told me. Thanks for following up.
